title: Real-time pseudo entropy and modular-Hamiltonian correlations
abstract: Pseudo entropy is a complex-valued generalization of entanglement entropy defined from a reduced transition matrix. We study the pseudo entropy associated with a real-time transition matrix between an initial pure state and its unitary time evolution. For a subsystem $A$, we show that the short-time behavior of real-time pseudo entropy is governed by the correlation between the physical Hamiltonian $H$ and the modular Hamiltonian $K_A=-\logρ_A$ of the initial reduced state, $ S_A(t,0)=S_A(0)-it \langle K_A(H-\langle H\rangle)\rangle + \mathcal{O}(t^2)$. For Hermitian dynamics, the initial imaginary response is controlled by the symmetrized covariance of $H$ and $K_A$ with an overall minus sign, while the initial real response is governed by their commutator. Thus the imaginary part of real-time pseudo entropy is not merely a branch artifact: it is a time-oriented modular response generated by the correlation between microscopic time evolution and subsystem coarse graining. We clarify the relation of this result to the known first law of pseudo entropy, derive an all-order expression in a Schmidt-diagonal model, recover thermal pseudo entropy as a special case, illustrate the covariance/commutator decomposition in a two-qubit model, and confirm the covariance response in transverse-field Ising-chain quenches, including a finite-size study of a modular susceptibility near the Ising critical region. We discuss how this amplitude-level oriented response can be related to ordinary entropy production, and also give a concrete $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric toy-model illustration of the non-Hermitian extension.
summary: This work introduces 'pseudo entropy,' a complex generalization of entanglement entropy used to track the directional flow of information during real-time quantum evolution. The key finding is that this pseudo entropy's short-time change decomposes into two parts: an imaginary component driven by modular covariance and a real component driven by commutators. This framework extends naturally to non-Hermitian physics, providing a powerful diagnostic for time-asymmetric quantum processes.
main_problem: To derive a microscopic, time-oriented entropic quantity (pseudo entropy) that captures directional information about quantum evolution before standard thermodynamic irreversibility is established.
main_result: The short-time change in real-time pseudo entropy splits into an imaginary part governed by the modular covariance of the Hamiltonian and initial state, and a real part governed by the commutator of these operators.
method: The analysis relies on calculating the time derivative of the pseudo entropy using the reduced transition matrix ($	au$) and decomposing this variation into covariance and commutator terms.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to general quantum systems undergoing real-time unitary evolution (quenches), with specific illustrations in two-qubit models, transverse-field Ising chains, and non-Hermitian PT-symmetric toy models.
key_observables: Real-time pseudo entropy ($S_A(t, 0)$), modular covariance response ($\propto \langle \{K_A, H\} angle$), and the commutator expectation value ($\langle [K_A, H] angle$).
important_parameters: Time $t$ (especially short-time expansion), temperature/inverse temperature $ eta$, and system size $L$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a definition of pseudo entropy via the reduced transition matrix and focuses on the leading order ($O(t^2)$) time dependence.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the real ($	ext{Re } S_A(t)$) and imaginary ($	ext{Im } S_A(t)$) components of the pseudo entropy after an Ising-chain quench, showing the linear imaginary response fixed by modular covariance. A finite-size study shows the modular susceptibility peaking near criticality.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first defining the complex pseudo entropy and deriving its short-time expansion. It then rigorously separates the time evolution into distinct contributions (covariance/commutator). The methodology is extended to non-Hermitian systems, culminating in discussions relating this oriented response to holographic principles.
why_interesting: It provides a novel, amplitude-level diagnostic tool for quantum dynamics that intrinsically carries an arrow of time, offering insights beyond standard entropy production theorems relevant to open and non-equilibrium quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Real and imaginary parts of the real-time pseudo entropy in the two-qubit model. We plot Re SA(t) −SA(0) and Im SA(t) for p = 0.3, q = 0.7, ϕ = π/4, and g = 1.2. Dashed lines show the linear predictions from Eqs. (62) and (63). The imaginary part is governed by the modular co- variance, while the real part is governed by the commutator expectation value.

FIG. 2. Real-time pseudo entropy after a transverse-field Ising-chain quench. The system is an open chain with L = 6, initial field hi = 1.0, final field hf = 1.55, and subsystem size LA = 3. The real part has no linear term for this real time- reversal-symmetric setup, while the imaginary part is linear with slope fixed by the modular covariance. Dashed lines show the first-order predictions.

FIG. 3. Finite-size modular susceptibility χA(h) in the open transverse-field Ising chain, Eq. (71), for L = 6, 8, 10 and LA = L/2. The vertical dotted line marks the thermodynamic critical point h = 1. The peak sharpens and moves toward the critical region as L increases, suggesting that the imaginary pseudo-entropy slope probes many-body critical correlations through the modular covariance.
